profile.reading: Arcola Tech Park is a commercial land development in eastern Loudoun County, Virginia, part of the St. John Properties portfolio, sited along John Mosby Highway (U.S. Route 50) near the newly built Northstar Boulevard, about two miles from Washington Dulles International Airport. Loudoun County is home to the world's densest cluster of data centers, and St. John Properties markets Arcola Tech Park specifically for that use, describing it in leasing materials as offering by right data center development potential across roughly 1.6 million square feet of buildable space, meaning a data center project there can generally proceed under existing zoning without a separate rezoning case. The broader tract also includes at least one outparcel being marketed for a convenience store rather than a data center. As of the most recent available mapping, the site carries a 2030 target opening date, consistent with a property still in the land planning and pre construction phase rather than an operating facility with a named tenant. No hyperscale or colocation operator has been publicly identified as having leased or purchased the site, and no building, power capacity, or square footage for an actual constructed data center has been published anywhere found in this research. This entry therefore describes a real, actively marketed by right data center development site in the heart of Data Center Alley, not yet a built and operating facility.

reading.body:
Arcola Tech Park is a permitted data center development site in Loudoun County, Virginia, marketed by St. John Properties for by-right construction across roughly 1.6 million square feet of buildable space. The site sits two miles from Washington Dulles International Airport along U.S. Route 50 in the heart of Data Center Alley, where Loudoun County hosts the world's densest cluster of data centers. No building has been constructed, no operator named, and no power or capacity specifications published. The site carries a 2030 target opening date and remains in the pre-construction planning phase.

Virginia hosts 330 mapped data center facilities, of which only 25 have published power capacity figures totaling 1603.4 megawatts. Arcola Tech Park is not among the 25 sites with published specifications and therefore does not rank in Virginia's operational capacity. This is a land position, not yet a source of grid load or AI compute.

The by-right zoning removes a significant regulatory delay that typically extends pre-construction timelines for data centers in other jurisdictions. Proximity to Dulles and to the interstate corridor offers network and transportation logistics advantages common to sites in the region. The development remains speculative until a named operator acquires the land and begins construction, at which point its actual power draw, capacity density, and grid impact will depend on the tenant's engineering and the state's ability to deliver power to the site.
